clue.text: Course created by a man from St Andrews?

parts.note: St Andrews is a town in Scotland, so a man from there is a Scot

explanation.surface: A golf course designed by a Scotsman, St Andrews being the famous home of golf.
explanation.walkthrough: St Andrews suggests golf, but the course is a racecourse: Ascot is the English racecourse near Windsor.
explanation.definitionFit: A racecourse is a course, and Ascot is a famous English example of one.

clue.text: Secretary uses name Susan, I fancy

indicators.note: fancy describes something elaborate or ornamented, so these letters are arranged differently

explanation.surface: A secretary makes use of a woman named Susan, the speaker suspects.
explanation.definitionFit: An amanuensis is a person who takes dictation or copies manuscripts, a literary assistant.

definitions.meaning: a Rodgers and Hammerstein stage show of 1945
the rotating belt at an airport that delivers luggage

explanation.definitionFit: The name of a stage musical and also the revolving airport luggage belt.

parts.note: fastest velocity, read as how fast a spinning toy goes

explanation.surface: The fastest a spinning cricket bowler can manage.
explanation.definitionFit: Fastest possible velocity is the phrase's sense, and a spinning toy is a top.

parts.note: a person first arrives in the world on the day they are born, celebrated each year

explanation.surface: Someone's scheduled arrival time, as at a station or airport.
explanation.definitionFit: The day of one's birth is literally the time one arrived in the world.
The word names brown horses and also means howls as a hound does.

parts.note: to take goods dishonestly, by stealing them

explanation.surface: To be oversensitive and misread what people say.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealing is taking things wrongfully, playing on the idiom for misunderstanding.

parts.note: a university qualification, which also names a unit of temperature or angle

explanation.surface: A policy introduced in schools.
explanation.definitionFit: A university award is an educational qualification, and the same word is a unit of measurement.

clue.text: Boys may turn into aggressive teenagers

indicators.note: the letters of the word boys turn into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A worry that young lads will grow into thugs.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for loutish, rowdy young people.

clue.text: Burly Pat reformed in a very sudden way

indicators.note: the letters of Burly and Pat are formed anew into a different order

explanation.surface: A burly man called Pat changed his ways suddenly.
explanation.definitionFit: Abruptly is an adverb meaning suddenly and without warning, a direct synonym.

parts.note: a team is a side, as in a football side
arms are limbs, members of the body

explanation.surface: The weapons belonging to the players in a team.
explanation.walkthrough: Members here are limbs of the body, not people on the team.
explanation.definitionFit: Sidearms are small weapons such as pistols worn at the belt.

parts.note: the money earned on a sum invested, capital meaning money rather than a city

explanation.surface: Coming back home from London.
explanation.definitionFit: Money paid on a loan or deposit is the yield earned on capital.

clue.text: Soft-hearted moneylender who enters office uninvited

indicators.note: Soft-hearted puts the soft letter in the heart, the middle, of the lender's word

parts.note: a usurer lends money at excessive interest
p (piano) is the musical abbreviation for soft

explanation.surface: A kindly moneylender who barges into an office without being asked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soft-hearted' looks like kindness, but it puts P (soft) into the heart of USURER.
explanation.definitionFit: A usurper seizes a position of power, such as a throne or post, without any right to it.

clue.text: Philosopher offers wine and gold when entertaining us

indicators.note: entertaining means holding a guest, so one word holds the other

parts.note: rosé is a pink wine
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A thinker hosts friends with pink wine and golden gifts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertaining' looks like hospitality but is the container signal; 'offers', 'and' and 'when' are only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Jacques Rousseau was the eighteenth-century Genevan thinker who wrote The Social Contract.

indicators.note: off describes something gone wrong or out of order, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone convalescing needs a month off work.
explanation.definitionFit: A common idiom for getting better after illness or a setback.

indicators.note: something misrepresented is shown wrongly, so these letters appear in a different arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone's commands were distorted in official decrees.
explanation.definitionFit: Instructions telling someone what to do are commands, a synonym of orders.

parts.note: a trader with exclusive rights is the only supplier; a fishmonger supplies a flatfish named sole

explanation.surface: A fish seller who has cornered the market.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm with exclusive selling rights is the only distributor, and the fishy twist reads the first word as the flatfish.

clue.text: Business leader takes a walk to see source of blackberries

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, here of Business

parts.note: rambles means goes for a country walk

explanation.surface: A company boss goes on a country stroll to find blackberries.
explanation.definitionFit: Blackberries grow on thorny shrubs of the genus Rubus, the plants that produce them.

definitions.meaning: settle firmly and begin to thrive
what a plant does below ground, not a reference to Australia

explanation.definitionFit: A plant grows anchoring growth below the soil, and the idiom means to settle in firmly.

clue.text: Ships in which sherry may be served

definitions.meaning: sailing vessels with fore-and-aft rigged masts

definitions.text: in which sherry may be served
definitions.meaning: tall glasses used in Britain for a large measure of sherry

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a type of sailing ship and a large sherry glass.

clue.text: It gives one who is stiff a ride

definitions.text: It gives one who is stiff a ride

parts.words: It gives one who is stiff a ride
parts.note: a stiff is slang for a corpse, carried to the funeral in a vehicle

explanation.surface: Something that offers a lift to someone with aching joints.
explanation.definitionFit: The vehicle that carries a coffin, taking the deceased (a stiff) on a final journey.

clue.text: Experts know them to be edible bulbs

definitions.text: Experts know them to be edible bulbs

parts.words: Experts know them to be edible bulbs
parts.note: alludes to the British idiom that experts know their stuff, phrased with a kitchen vegetable

explanation.surface: Specialists can tell which plant bulbs are safe to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Edible bulbs used as a vegetable, and the British saying that someone who is expert 'knows their' these.

clue.text: Marks exercises during exam, causing uproar

indicators.note: during places these pieces within the time of the exam word

parts.note: a test is an exam
M is the abbreviation for the mark, the old German currency
PE is physical education, school exercises

explanation.surface: A teacher marks the PE exercises taken during an exam, provoking an outcry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' is the container signal; the old German mark is abbreviated M.
explanation.definitionFit: A tempest is a violent storm, and figuratively a furious commotion or tumult.

definitions.meaning: polite and pleasantly considerate in manner
an exclamation of surprise, as in Good heavens or Goodness

explanation.definitionFit: The word means polite and kind, and also serves as the exclamation of surprise 'good ...!'

parts.note: a miss is a girl, a gal

explanation.surface: A young woman heads off to a festival.
explanation.definitionFit: A gala is a festive celebration or special public entertainment.

clue.text: Singer who is said never to give an encore

definitions.text: Singer who is said never to give an encore

parts.words: Singer who is said never to give an encore
parts.note: legend has a bird singing only once, just before death, hence a final performance

explanation.surface: A vocalist who reportedly refuses to perform again.
explanation.definitionFit: The mute bird is said to sing only once, as it dies, hence the phrase for a final performance.

parts.note: a well is made by boring into the ground
a to-do is a task, as on a to-do list

explanation.surface: A dull chore suited to wealthy people.
explanation.definitionFit: Being comfortably wealthy is the meaning of this hyphenated adjective.

parts.note: a version is a translation of a text into another language

explanation.surface: A poor translation that makes readers dislike the book.
explanation.definitionFit: Aversion is a strong dislike, a direct synonym of antipathy.

clue.text: Grounds which are worth seeing, one hears

indicators.note: one hears signals that the word is spoken, giving a word of identical sound

parts.note: sights are things worth seeing, as tourist attractions

explanation.surface: Places with attractive views, according to word of mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Grounds and sites are both pieces of land set aside for a purpose.
